sentences.text: Ruyangosaurus is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur found in the Early Cretaceous Haoling Formation of China, though its fossils were recovered from the Mangchuan Formation in Ruyang County, Henan Province.
In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated Ruyangosaurus reached a length of 30 meters and a weight of over 50 tonnes, classifying it as a 'mega-sauropod'.
Another estimate suggests Ruyangosaurus was about 35 meters long, based on a 207 cm femur and a 127 cm right tibia.
The type species Ruyangosaurus giganteus was described in 2009 by Lü Junchang and colleagues.
In 2020, Molina-Perez and Larramendi provided a lower size estimate of 24.8 meters in length and 34 tonnes in weight.

The original describers assigned Ruyangosaurus to Andesauridae, but this family is no longer used because it is not monophyletic; a smaller phylogenetic dataset based on additional material from the type locality found Ruyangosaurus to be a non-titanosauriform macronarian, while the Paleobiology Database lists the parent group as Euhelopodidae.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Ruyangosaurus as Euhelopodidae.
Ruyangosaurus lived during the Aptian to Albian stages, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
It is debated whether Ruyangosaurus is a somphospondyl or a non-titanosauriform macronarian closely related to Yunmenglong, as different phylogenetic datasets yield conflicting results.
